findings.evidence: The new favourite prefill (lines 269-276, 567-570) saves a planned game expense whose start_date/end_date are the schedule period while target_date is schedule.start_date, and schedule_id is the official VERSION that contains that date (matchingVersion, line 554). When that expense is later edited from /dashboard/expenses (expenses/page.tsx:641-654 passes start_date/end_date), edit mode infers `isVersionPass = start_date !== end_date` (lines 217-222). On save, `isVersionPass && matchingVersion` (line 563) rewrites start/end to the VERSION period and target_date to the VERSION end_date; if no version matches, the else branch collapses the period to the payment date because prefillPeriod is reset to null on open. Example: PICKUP 11-12..11-25 inside VERSION 11-05..12-03 -> saved as 11-12..11-25 (target 11-12); editing only the price saves 11-05..12-03 with target 12-03.
findings.impact: Editing any planned expense created from a favourite non-pass schedule silently moves its payment/target date and period (and with it the budget month it is attributed to) and shows the version-pass checkbox as checked, although the user never chose a version pass.
findings.recommendation: Make edit-mode pass detection distinguish real version passes (e.g. treat as pass only when start_date !== end_date AND target_date === end_date, which is how version-pass rows are written at line 566), and keep a non-pass row's stored start/end period on edit while its date is unchanged (same rule as prefillPeriod). Add a Vitest case: open edit mode with {target 11-12, start 11-12, end 11-25} and a matching VERSION, save, and assert the update payload keeps target/start/end and that the pass checkbox is unchecked.

findings.evidence: For a favourite VERSION schedule the spec requires `schedule_id = schedule.id`, but the prefill only sets the date and relies on `matchingVersion = schedules.find(s => s.start_date <= paymentDate && paymentDate <= s.end_date)` over versions ordered by start_date. If the previous version's end_date is on or after the favourite version's start_date (versions that hand over on maintenance day), the previous version is found first. ExpensePrefill (lines 67-75) does not carry the schedule id, so the modal cannot prefer it.
findings.impact: The planned expense can be linked to and labelled with the wrong (previous) version, and later version date edits sync it through the wrong schedule.
findings.recommendation: Add an optional `schedule_id` to ExpensePrefill (set only for VERSION schedules) and let matchingVersion prefer that schedule while paymentDate lies within its period; cover the touching-boundary case in expense-modal.test.tsx.

findings.evidence: handleToggleFavorite, the favourite loader and the missing-table check are duplicated almost verbatim in src/app/dashboard/games/page.tsx:470-540. Neither copy guards in-flight writes, so a quick second click on the same star sends delete and insert concurrently and the optimistic local state can end opposite to the server until reload.
findings.impact: Low: rare visual mismatch after rapid double clicks, and two copies to keep in sync.
findings.recommendation: Optionally extract a small shared hook (e.g. useFavoriteSchedules(userId)) and ignore toggles for a schedule id whose write is still pending. Can be deferred.
